oneStopSecurity.note: Air France: no security checkpoint after a flight from a Schengen country, Canada, the United States, Ireland or the United Kingdom (ev:cdg-af-transit-security). The other EU states (Cyprus) and EEA follow from EU law. Montenegro, Singapore and the Faroe Islands are in the EU list but not in Air France's: left out at CDG (conservative). Tel Aviv arrivals are re-screened (Reg. 2025/920).

deadline.text: El Al (Jan 2023 notice, relayed): hand-baggage-only passengers at the gate 50 min before departure; current validity unknown

specialScreening.text: El Al departs from Terminal 2B (feed: all 7 LY TLV departures report terminal 2B) and runs its security check at the gate; connecting passengers are questioned at the gate (2023 notice relay; 2026 traveller report). Time of the check not published.

Air France Tel Aviv flights (2E) have a 90-min check-in deadline (published) but no current published extra screening; Arkia uses Terminal 3. Whether other Israel flights have an extra check at CDG is not established.

US-bound flights: TSA / DHS enhanced security measures for all last-point-of-departure airports (2017, still the baseline as far as known) may add checks at check-in or at the gate (interviews, document checks, separate screening of electronics). The procedures are not public; no time is known.

rules.text: Border zones by building: 2A, 2C, 2E (K, L, M) and the 2B gates are non-Schengen; 2F and 2G serve Schengen flights; 2D is the Schengen side of the shared 2B/2D area (D50–D69 kept mixed); T1 gates 10–38 non-Schengen and 40–68 Schengen (2026 first-hand); T3 has one lounge with border police for non-Schengen flights.

Controls by connection type (guide, 2026): Schengen → Schengen none; Schengen → non-Schengen passport; non-Schengen → Schengen passport and security; non-Schengen → non-Schengen security (unless one-stop security applies). Entering the Schengen area needs entry eligibility, airside too.

Checked bags and customs. One ticket: bags are transferred automatically and the passenger stays in the transit area; "Les passagers sont informés à l'aéroport de départ s'ils doivent récupérer leurs bagages à CDG ou à destination finale" (CDG Facile, 2026-10-29). Separate tickets or re-check: collect the bags, leave to the public zone (entry passport control after a non-Schengen flight, then customs), check in at the departure terminal, then security and, for non-Schengen flights, exit passport control; there is no check-in desk in the transit area. Hold-baggage customs (EU Implementing Regulation 2015/2447 art. 39): after a flight from outside the EU, hold baggage transferred onto an intra-EU flight is cleared at the last international EU airport of that flight; when the onward flight goes to another international airport of the same Member State (for example a French domestic flight) the controls may be carried out at the transfer airport. Whether CDG applies this, so that bags are reclaimed at CDG on international → French domestic connections, is not established (q:cdg-dom-bags). From 00:00 to 04:00 the Terminal 2 public zones are open only to passengers with a boarding pass (CDG Facile). The model times movement only: baggage reclaim, check-in and bag drop are not included.

One-stop security: transfer screening is waived when the previous flight was screened at an airport the EU recognises; Air France lists Schengen countries, Canada, the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom. EU Regulation 2025/920 removed Tel Aviv Ben Gurion, so Tel Aviv arrivals are re-screened.

No airside Schengen path links 2D with 2F/2G (contradicted by 2B/2D signage): Schengen 2D ↔ 2F/2G connections go through the public side. 2G is reached airside only by the orange shuttle from 2F (Schengen) and publicly by the N2 bus.

Phase 2: the purple line is routed as the 2F → Hall M bus (05:30–20:00, probable identification). Yellow (2G ↔ 2E K) and red (2G – 2F east – 2E M) are drawn with notRouted: listed on the official map (2026-10-28) and by Air France / ADP, but no first-hand ride and no documented border-control position. Grey (2G ↔ 2E L) and green (T1 ↔ 2A/2C) have no stop on the current Terminal 2 map and are not drawn.

Movement times here are not connection times. Air France minimum connection time at CDG is 60 min (80 min in some cases, pilot finding PR); the airport recommends 90 min within T1 / Terminal 2, 120 min T1 ↔ T2 and 2A–2F ↔ 2G, 150 min T1 ↔ 2G (relay of the official page, 2026-09).

From 16 March 2027 the terminals are renamed: T1 → Terminal 1, T3 → Terminal 2, 2A/2C → Terminal 3, 2B/2D → Terminal 4, 2E → Terminal 5 (K → D, L → C, M → B), 2F → Terminal 6, 2G → Terminal 7, with new one-letter gate prefixes. The old → new gate-number mapping is not published, so this model keeps the current numbers.

EES has been fully operational since 10 April 2026; PARAFE e-gates serve EU citizens with biometric documents and some third-country nationals. Border allowances here are planning values, not queue predictions.

Night (01:00–04:00): CDGVAL is closed and replaced by buses outside the stations (ADP PDF, CDG Facile; stops and headway not published); N1 runs every 15 min 01:30–04:00 on the Terminal 2 public side. No airside line runs: LISA 04:30–00:30, blue 05:30–23:30, orange 05:30–23:00, purple 05:30–20:00, N2 05:30–23:30. Halls L and M are reachable only by LISA, so they are unroutable 00:30–04:30.

Phase 2: controls are counted once per physical checkpoint. A second security check is kept only where the passenger re-enters screening: after leaving airside (T1 Schengen via the public side), at Hall L/M (every LISA arrival is screened at the hall), at the 2B/2D stop for riders continuing into 2D (first-hand 2026), and at the 2B side of the 2B/2D stop (assumed).
